replacements.proposed_replacement:
Close and ordinary preclosure routing remain strict about the actual current manifest: its full bytes must equal the captured current archive. Neither the continuity registry nor a frozen close receipt may be rewritten after closure.

Later `step3-close verify` and postclosure `validateDownstreamConsumerRoute` authenticate history separately. Only an already marked original version-3 closure supplies the exact frozen artifact map. Every continuity registry and original reference must remain in that same sealed map with its original digest. Each canonical manifest artifact slot is reconstructed from its existing hash-bound closure-time current archive; this is a historical binding, never a claim that its old digest describes later live bytes. The full original/historical identity, native Alpha completion and root reconciliation checks still apply to those archived captures. No new postclosure archive, certificate or repair route may enlarge the frozen artifact set. All other artifacts retain their ordinary exact-current-byte verification, and the exact artifact-set and ledger checks remain unchanged.

Postclosure route validation selects the artifact map only from the actual on-disk, same-run, closed version-3 receipt with the original dependency-ordered basis and marked manifest policy. The shared history helper authenticates that supplied map against the actual receipt and all sealed references/captures. Before closure or for an unmarked receipt, route validation retains strict live preclosure behavior; close/default artifact reconstruction never auto-selects the historical map.

The later live manifest is retained separately for actual target membership, unique current ownership/draft/run and direct-dependency checks in the downstream loader. This verifies historical closure without adopting a current source review or licensing any later mathematical or metadata repair. Unmarked receipts and close/default preclosure callers retain their original behavior.
